description: A sleek, handle-free galley kitchen shot in a strong one-point perspective from a standing eye-level, lens reading normal to slightly wide at roughly 28-35mm, looking straight down the corridor toward the far wall. The composition is centered and symmetrical, with both flanking cabinet runs converging on a single vanishing point at the end of the countertop line. Floor-to-ceiling cabinetry in a deep charcoal with a subtle horizontal wood-grain texture fills both sides completely, the flat slab fronts carrying no hardware. White Carrara-style marble-look quartz countertops run the full length on both sides, their cool veined surface catching a warm continuous band of illumination along the underside of the upper cabinets — a golden horizontal glow washing the backsplash and countertop surface. The backsplash is the same white stone-look material, seamless and clean. A black matte mixer tap anchors the right-side sink; a matte black induction cooktop sits beside it. On the left upper tower column, two stainless steel built-in ovens are stacked, their glossy glass faces reflecting the ambient room light. Countertop accessories are restrained: a compact potted green plant in a grey concrete pot, a stainless electric kettle, a glass carafe, a low matte bowl in charcoal, and a small brass-toned vessel. The floor is large-format cream porcelain tile laid in a simple grid. The ceiling is smooth white plaster. The mood is quiet and precise — deeply modern, confidently minimal.
